# 209 of 213 by-path test loaders are not cache-first, on keys shared by up to 9 files

## Provenance

Measured by AST walk over `tests/` while auditing bug 2bc7 (which repaired three files sharing the
`"mutation"` key). The audit's scope was that key; this is the surface it revealed.

```
total by-path loaders under tests/  : 213
using sys.modules.setdefault        :   0   (the original 9f0b/2bc7 defect is eradicated)
cache-first (name AND __file__)     :   4
```

The four are `test_differ.py`, `test_differ_conflict_resolution.py`,
`REDACTED_TOKEN.py` (2bc7's three) and `test_reconcile_filter.py::_stub_modules`.
2bc7 additionally fixed `test_differ_emits_probe.py` and `test_apply_list_of_mutations.py`.

## The collision surface

`sys.modules` keys registered by more than one test file:

```
outbound_differ   9 files        mutation    6 files
inbound_differ    8 files        reconcile   4 files
differ            5 files        applier     3 files
```

**None** of the loaders for `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `reconcile` or `applier` validates
`__file__`. The original bug surfaced on `mutation` only because that is where a cross-file
`isinstance` assertion happened to exist — the same latent coupling sits on keys with more registrants
and no such assertion to expose it.

## Why this is latent rather than broken

pytest executes module-by-module, so a file that overwrites a shared key is self-consistent while its
own tests run: its module-scoped fixture was built when its registration was current. The failure needs
two things to coincide — a cross-file identity comparison, and an execution order that puts the other
registrant first. 2bc7 was exactly that coincidence, and it presented as a macOS-only `isinstance`
failure on an object that WAS of the asserted class.

## What 2bc7 deliberately did not attempt

A shared helper, so the loader exists once. It is the right fix and it is not mechanical: the
registrants span `diffing/`, `mutate/`, `apply/`, `state/`, `fetch/`, `conflict/` and `orchestrate/`,
and pytest puts only each test's OWN directory on `sys.path`, so a bare-name import does not resolve
across them. Two workable shapes, both with costs:

* a module at the `tests/` root plus the `sys.path` plumbing `tests/_engine_path.py` already
  establishes — works for every caller including module-level constants;
* a conftest FIXTURE — inherited by subdirectories automatically, but cannot serve the call sites that
  load at module scope, and several do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ONE cache-first by-path loader exists, reachable from every directory under `tests/` that needs
      it, with the `sys.path` mechanism it depends on documented at its definition
- [ ] every loader registering a key that MORE THAN ONE file registers is converted to it — the
      `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `differ`, `mutation`, `reconcile` and `applier` keys at
      minimum
- [ ] a guard test fails when a new by-path loader registers a SHARED key without validating
      `__file__`, so the count cannot regress silently (the audit above was a one-off scan; a scan
      nobody re-runs is not a guard)
- [ ] loaders that deliberately want an ISOLATED copy keep it, and say so — `test_mutation.py`
      returns an unregistered private copy and `test_differ.py` registers
      `mutation_for_diff_purity` under a distinct name; both are correct and must not be swept into
      the shared helper
- [ ] the full suite passes under a REVERSED collection order for the affected directories, not just
      the default alphabetical one

## Not urgent, and why

Nothing fails today. This is a latent-coupling cleanup whose value is that the next instance fails
locally and deterministically instead of as a platform-specific surprise in CI.

# Addendum: 5-requirement re-evaluation + OSS-validated pattern recommendation

User pinned 5 core requirements: (1) never review a huge diff in one review; (2) accumulate a huge feature off-main, land it all at once; (3) every change reaching main passed LLM review; (4) no invalidation fragility from content-comparison or merge/rebase instability; (5) pattern must be OSS-validated, not novel/Frankenstein. Note (4)+(5) eliminate the prior options: TRIVIAL_REBASE vote-carry IS content comparison; a custom narrowed interaction re-review IS a novel invention; current chain+topic fails (4) (rebases wipe votes).

## Recommendation: Gerrit server-side feature branches + reviewed merge change (the OpenDev-documented pattern)

Stories = small reviewed changes targeting refs/heads/feature/<name>, merged into the branch AS they pass (attestation consumed immediately into branch history — no vote ever needs to survive a rebase; branch history is the durable accumulator, not label state). Feature completion = one --no-ff merge commit of the branch into main, pushed to refs/for/main as its own reviewed "merge change", gated by the same submit requirement, submitted atomically. No rebases anywhere → requirement 4 by construction.

## OSS validation (web-research agent, 2026-07-01, URLs in agent report)
- OpenDev/OpenStack: Infra Manual documents the exact flow (server-side branch via UI; pushMerge ACL; git merge --no-ff + push refs/for/master). LIVE: openstack/swift feature/mpu + feature/threaded active 2025-2026 with story-sized reviewed changes + monthly reviewed master->feature catch-up merges; merge changes carry the standard label gate (change 983874: Verified+2/CR+2/Workflow+1).
- Qt: reviewed merge changes live on codereview.qt-project.org (qt-creator origin/20.0->master merges June 2026); caveat: Qt abandoned ROUTINE cross-branch merges for release maintenance in 2020 (QUIP-16) in favor of cherry-picks — different use case (long-lived release branches) than finite feature branches.
- Wikimedia: ad-hoc merge commits into master confirmed; not documented policy.
- Chromium/AOSP/Go: deliberately linear (chains/topics/CQ) — the alternative school; their objection (merges hide interaction cost, hurt bisect) is the pattern's known weakness, mitigated by CI on the merge change.

## Three corrections vs assumptions
1. Human UI default diff base for merge commits is FIRST_PARENT (whole feature diff), not Auto Merge — auto-merge (conflict-resolutions-only) is a dropdown selection; server default confirmed in Gerrit source (GeneralPreferencesInfo.java). REST default IS auto-merge.
2. BOT TRAP: GET /changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/patch on a merge commit returns HTTP 409 ("Revision has more than 1 parent", GetPatch.java); patch?parent=1 returns the ENTIRE feature diff (violates req 1). No /patch variant gives vs-auto-merge. The bot must branch on parent count and use files/ (no parent param => auto-merge base) + per-file /diff (auto-merge base) + /mergelist. TODAY our voter would 409 -> fail-closed -1 on any merge change (safe failure, but blocks the pattern).
3. Gerrit has a purpose-built changekind MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE ("don't want to trigger CI or human verification again if your target branch moved forward", config-labels.html): add to LLM-Review copyCondition so re-merging after main advances doesn't wipe the vote; a new feature-tip is a REWORK and correctly re-reviews.

## Scorecard (feature-branch pattern): req1 PASS (story diffs small; merge change reviews conflict-delta vs auto-merge; caveat: textually-clean semantic conflicts show EMPTY auto-merge diff — CI on the merge change is the mitigation => open epic smoky-flare-slug/1fa8 Verified vote becomes a required complement, not optional). req2 PASS (feature branches live only in Gerrit; replication pushes main+tags only). req3 PASS (submit requirement has no branch clause — already gates feature branches; every commit reaching main was gated as story change or merge change). req4 PASS (no rebases; votes consumed at story-merge; MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE is Gerrit-native + doc-sanctioned). req5 PASS (OpenDev documented + live; honest caveats recorded).

## RED/BLUE/GREEN replay under the pattern
RED: change A -> feature branch, +1, submit into branch. BLUE: change B likewise (parallel worktrees fine — both target the branch; MERGE_IF_NECESSARY merges siblings without rebase). GREEN: pulls branch (A+B in history), builds C, small review, submit. Merge change to main: usually near-empty auto-merge delta + mergelist + CI. Zero re-review of A/B/C. Zero vote wipes.

## Concrete deltas to implement
a. infra/gerrit/project.config: copyCondition = "changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE"; [submit] explicit mergeContent=true + pin submitType=MERGE_IF_NECESSARY (currently unset/inherited — was already flagged); ACL: Create Reference + Delete Reference on refs/heads/feature/*; Push Merge Commit on refs/for/refs/heads/main + refs/for/refs/heads/feature/*.
b. src/rebar/review_bot/: merge-change code path (detect via revisions/{rev}/commit parents length; assemble review input from files/ + per-file diff vs auto-merge + mergelist; keep fail-closed).
c. keep receive.rejectImplicitMerges compatible (it does NOT block explicit merge commits — config-project-config.html).
d. CONTRIBUTING.md + docs: feature-branch workflow (OpenDev recipe incl. Change-Id amend), branch-lifetime cap, scheduled catch-up merges, branch deletion after merge-back (no Gerrit auto-cleanup exists).
e. smoky-flare-slug (CI Verified vote): elevate to required for merge changes (auto-merge diff cannot catch semantic conflicts).

# Eval corpus + ADR-0054 calibration for `project.measurement-provenance`

## Context

Story `f161-c70a-1a69-4ed1` landed the measurement-provenance mechanism: the deterministic
presence/shape check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`, advisory via `p6_ac_quality`), the
`.rebar/` overlay routing entry (advisory, `exec: AGENT`, `[operator-attested]` trigger), the
`execution_mode: agentic` rubric stating decision rules (a)-(d), and ADR-0061.

What it did NOT deliver is any proof that the AGENT criterion actually FIRES or STAYS SILENT as
the rubric specifies. The rubric states the rules; nothing exercises them. Every sibling project
criterion ships a `.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml`; this one has none.

This was descoped from f161 deliberately: the criterion ships **advisory**, so the mechanism is
correct and useful without calibration, and the ADR-0054 promotion decision it feeds is not being
made yet. Filed as an **idea** because promotion is a judgement call nobody has committed to.

## Approach

Follow the `project.engine-layer-enforcement` pattern exactly (`.rebar/evals/REDACTED_TOKEN.eval.yaml`
+ its offline shape test + a live semantic run recorded as attested evidence).

**1. `.rebar/evals/REDACTED_TOKEN.eval.yaml`** — a BALANCED corpus,
`epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, a deterministic `emits_valid_findings` scorer. Each entry needs a
`note` naming the causal mechanism and observable effect, not just a label. Minimum fixtures:

| Rule | Fixture | expect |
|---|---|---|
| (a) environment contradiction | declares `579718921998`, repo Terraform backend names `896586841071` | finding |
| (a) contrast | declared account MATCHES the IaC | pass |
| (b) no-anchor fallback | non-AWS cluster/tenant id with no in-repo counterpart | pass |
| (c) privilege posture | scoped-permission criterion declaring `privilege_posture=broader` | finding |
| (c) contrast | same criterion declaring `production-equivalent` | pass |
| (d) instrument vs claim | AUTHORIZATION claim + `instrument=simulation` **at** `privilege_posture=production-equivalent` | finding |
| (d) contrast | same claim with `instrument=live-call` | pass |

The (d) must-fire case is the load-bearing one: it is the ONLY fixture that proves `instrument` is
judged INDEPENDENTLY of `privilege_posture`. Both fields read 'fine' in it, and it must still fire —
that is escape 2b (`simulate-principal-policy` returning a confident WRONG authorization answer that
only a live call refuted). If this fixture passes when it should fire, the fourth field epic 3147
mandated is decorative.

**Fixture quality is the actual work.** A must-fire plan so obviously broken that any criterion
would flag it proves nothing. Each must-fire case should differ from its contrast case in ONE
declared field, so a fire/pass split isolates the rule under test.

**2. `tests/unit/REDACTED_TOKEN.py`** — offline shape checks, no LLM, CI-safe:
fixture parses, ids unique, `criterion` matches, both polarities present, every rule covered.

**3. Live semantic run** — `rebar criteria eval project.measurement-provenance --runs 3`, recorded on
this ticket as `[operator-attested]` evidence. Dogfood this epic's own contract: the attestation must
itself carry a `provenance:` line (environment / principal / privilege_posture / instrument), which
doubles as the cheapest possible test that the new four-field contract is writable in practice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the eval corpus exists with BOTH polarities for each of rules (a), (c) and (d), plus the
      rule-(b) no-anchor pass case, each carrying a `note` naming the causal mechanism
- [ ] the rule-(d) must-fire fixture declares `privilege_posture=production-equivalent` AND
      `instrument=simulation` on an authorization claim, proving `instrument` is judged
      independently rather than as a proxy for privilege
- [ ] each must-fire fixture differs from its contrast fixture in exactly ONE declared field, so
      the fire/pass split isolates the rule under test
- [ ] an OFFLINE shape test passes with no LLM call: `pytest tests/unit/REDACTED_TOKEN.py -q`
- [ ] [operator-attested] the live run `rebar criteria eval project.measurement-provenance --runs 3`
      is recorded on this ticket with its per-fixture outcomes and the measured FALSE-POSITIVE RATE,
      and that comment itself carries a `provenance:` line declaring environment, principal,
      privilege_posture and instrument (dogfooding ADR-0061)
- [ ] the promotion decision is RECORDED either way: advisory -> blocking with the FP rate that
      justifies it, or 'stays advisory' with the reason — ADR-0054 requires the evidence, not a
      particular outcome

### The tension
rebar deliberately BIN-PACKS same-facet Pass-1 criteria into one LLM call (a 'chunk') for cost + prompt-cache efficiency, accepting cross-criterion contamination WITHIN a chunk, and relies on the independent Pass-2 verifier + deterministic arithmetic to filter contamination artifacts. ### The proposal (converged in design discussion)
A CONFIG FLAG, not a rewrite:
- Default (flag off) = current bin-packing. No behavior change; back-out is flipping it off.
- Flag on = every BLOCKING-ELIGIBLE criterion executes in its OWN isolated context window (co-residency = 1), so the highest-stakes findings (the only ones that can block a claim) are never contaminated by chunk neighbors. The advisory tail stays bin-packed (bounded cost).
- Rationale: spend isolation cost ONLY where a wrong finding changes an outcome (blocks a claim) -- same 'spend rigor where it matters' logic as the 0.70 blocking threshold and R-2 targeted redundancy.

### Evidence gate (why this is deferred, not built now)
rebar's STATED position is that the Pass-2 verifier already catches contamination. This proposal bets that verifier-catching is imperfect for blocking findings -- a bet that must be TESTED before building. It depends on the R-1 part-1 'cohort' observability field (shipping in the main DSO-adoption epic): each Pass-1 finding gets stamped with its chunk cohort (sorted criterion-id set) in pass1_chunk (passes.py:294-306), carried through _slim (sidecar.py:236-264). Flip this flag on (like novelty_drop_active / completion_floor_active) only after cohort analysis clears the bar.

CONDITIONALLY, and the condition is inverted from what anyone would assume: they read as covered
everywhere, and they break precisely where the optional extra IS installed — i.e. exactly the
environment where their coverage was supposed to matter. A skip is masking a defect rather than
representing an absent capability.

fallback arm to direct Anthropic fails immediately with an auth error, so the chain provides

TWO DURABLE LESSONS FOR THIS CELL, which is why they belong here rather than on that change:

1. **A test entering that app's lifespan silently inherits a 20-minute shutdown drain plus a real filesystem sweep.** The py3.11 cell is therefore unusually sensitive to any new `TestClient(app)` CONTEXT-MANAGER use in that module. A lint or fixture guard — requiring the `reconcile_loop` stub whenever the lifespan is entered — would be cheap insurance against re-introducing a 20-minute hang.

2. **The two failure modes are distinguishable from the log alone, without bisecting.** The HANG mode ends at a progress percentage with orphaned `pytest`/`python` children and NO summary line. The WORKER-CRASH mode names the test and the `gw<N>` worker. That is enough to route a future occurrence to the right cause immediately — which matters, because they need opposite responses: the hang wants a code fix, the crash has so far only wanted a retry.

This does NOT reclassify the occurrences recorded above. The 1520 worker-crash instances and the 1512 PS7 crash remain unattributed to any diff (untouched file, passes locally, cleared on a content-free rebase). What changes is the general claim: 'a py3.11 hang means the runner' is WRONG as a heuristic. Distinguish the two modes by signature first.
